_comment: Hoenn & Seek 2.1-31: DAN's episodes (the history broadcaster at the PEWTER MUSEUM, 2F).
Read by tools/hoenn/gen_hoenn_dan.py, which writes data/scripts/hoenn_dan_texts.inc (the
message texts, word-wrapped like the hint lines) and src/data/hoenn_dan.h (the table
episodes: in the order he tells them, one new episode a week. Never reorder or remove one:
VAR_HOENN_DAN_EPISODE saves an index. Append only.
title: the episode's name (menus and the radio), at most 18 characters.
parts: the installments, one per talk (at most 4). Each is a list of strings, one message
box each (wrapped at 34 characters; keep a box to three lines or so).
teaser: what he says at the end of the episode before this one ('Next week...'). The first
radio: his PokéGear show's lines about it (PLACES AND PEOPLE), wrapped at 30 characters,
lines: his fixed lines (see its own _comment). outro: what he says after the last episode, instead of a teaser.
These lines are drafts until the 2.1-36c dialogue pass with Bryan.

episodes.title: WORDS IN STONE
parts: Picture a valley in JOHTO. Three thousand years ago, maybe more. No roads. No POKé BALLS.
People come to the RUINS with chisels and lamps, and they carve the same strange shapes into the walls. Over and over.
Why? You don't spend a whole life in the dark on decoration.
They were writing something down. Something they were afraid the world would forget.
Here's what keeps me up at night. The shapes on those walls... move.
The UNOWN. Twenty-six of them, then two more. Each one looks exactly like a letter on the wall.
Did the people copy the POKéMON? Or did the POKéMON climb out of the writing?
Think about being the first person to watch a word peel itself off a stone and float away.
Scholars spent a century on those walls. The answer came from somewhere nobody looked: the radio.
Tune in near the RUINS and you hear a signal. It's the UNOWN. Talking. Or reading aloud.
Some say the walls are a library, and the UNOWN are librarians who never went home.
And if they're still reading... who are they reading to?
episodes.radio: The UNOWN, and the people who carved them into the walls.

episodes.title: THE TOWER BURNS
teaser: Next week: a tower, a storm, and three POKéMON nobody would ever have remembered.
parts: ECRUTEAK. Two towers, built to face each other across the town. The BRASS TOWER and the TIN TOWER.
They weren't built for show. They were meant as a meeting place between people and POKéMON.
For about a hundred and fifty years, it worked. A great rainbow bird roosted on the BRASS TOWER.
Then one night, lightning. Some say it was only a storm. Some say it wasn't.
The tower burned for three days. Imagine standing in the street, watching the beams come down.
Three POKéMON were caught inside. No names. Nobody would ever have remembered them.
When the rain finally came, a rainbow-colored POKéMON came down out of it.
It brought the three back. Not as they were. As something new: thunder, fire and the north wind.
Then it flew off, and it never came back to the BRASS TOWER. Who could blame it?
We call the three RAIKOU, ENTEI and SUICUNE. They're still running. Maybe they're still looking for it.
episodes.radio: The night the BRASS TOWER burned, and what came out of the fire.

episodes.title: WHEN SEAS ROSE
teaser: Next week we go further back than anyone was there to see. Land against sea.
parts: Go back further. Before towns. Before people. HOENN was only land and sea, and each had a master.
GROUDON raised the land. KYOGRE filled the sea.
And neither one thought the other had any business existing.
So they fought. Not like a POKéMON battle. Like weather.
Drought that split the rock in two. Rain that never, ever stopped.
Say you're alive back then, on some little ledge of land. Which one do you pray for?
Think about it. Either answer drowns somebody.
It ended from above. A green serpent came down out of the sky and roared until both of them stopped.
RAYQUAZA. It didn't win. It just ended the fight. The two of them went to sleep, under the earth and under the sea.
Look at a map of HOENN, {PLAYER}. Every coastline is the place they stopped. It's a map of a truce.
episodes.radio: GROUDON, KYOGRE, and the day the sky told them both to stop.

episodes.title: THE KING'S WEAPON
teaser: Next week: a land far from here, a king, and a grief so big it ended a war.
parts: Far from here there's a land called KALOS. Three thousand years ago, it was at war.
A king there had a POKéMON he loved more than anything.
It was taken from him to fight. It never came home.
The king couldn't accept it. He built a machine to bring it back to life. And it worked.
But grief is never satisfied. He turned the machine into a weapon. And he used it.
It ended the war. It ended everyone on both sides of the war.
The story says the POKéMON he saved left him once it saw what he'd done.
Think about that. To save one life you love, you burn a whole country. And the one you saved can't look at you.
The king, they say, is still alive somewhere. Still waiting. I hope that part isn't true.
episodes.radio: KALOS, a king who lost his POKéMON, and the weapon he built.

episodes.title: THE FIRST DAY
teaser: Next week we start before anything started at all. Bring a snack.
parts: Every people has a story of how the world began. JOHTO's oldest one is carved at the SINJOH RUINS.
Before anything, there was an egg. Out of the egg came one POKéMON. The carvings give it a thousand arms.
It made time, and space. And a third thing nobody likes to talk about: whatever is on the other side.
Three dragons. Then the spirits of the lakes, of knowledge and feeling and will.
Then it went to sleep. Its work was done.
But read the carvings closely and they say something more. It made people a promise.
It would come back one day, to see what the world had made of itself.
Imagine being the one standing there when it opens its eyes. What do you say to the one who made everything?
episodes.radio: The SINJOH RUINS, an egg, and the POKéMON that made the world.

episodes.title: THE ROCKET YEARS
teaser: Next week, the last one: a story you might know better than I do.
parts: Let's come closer to home. Living memory. TEAM ROCKET.
It started under the GAME CORNER in CELADON. A boss with a big plan, and an even bigger organization behind him.
Stolen POKéMON. Experiments. They even took SILPH CO. by force.
And who stopped them? Not the police. Not the LEAGUE. A kid from PALLET TOWN with a POKéDEX.
The boss was a GYM LEADER, if you can believe it. He lost, and he walked away.
His team didn't. Years later they took over the RADIO TOWER in GOLDENROD and called for him on the air.
He never answered. Some say he heard and chose not to.
Then another kid stopped them all over again. A kid from NEW BARK TOWN. Sound familiar, {PLAYER}?
History isn't only old stones. Someday somebody will tell your story on the radio.
What do you want them to say?
episodes.radio: TEAM ROCKET, from the GAME CORNER to the RADIO TOWER.

lines._comment: His fixed lines, as HoennSeek_Text_Dan_<Key> (data/scripts/hoenn_dan.inc uses them). STR_VAR_1 = episode number, STR_VAR_2 = title, STR_VAR_3 = installment number.
Intro: Oh! A visitor. Come in, come in. The name's DAN.
I tell stories. Old ones. The kind that happened to real people and real POKéMON, who had no idea anyone would ever remember them.
I do a show on the radio, THE DEEP PAST. But I like telling it to somebody's face better.
One story a week, a piece at a time. Ready? Let's begin.
Continue: Back for more? Good. {STR_VAR_2}, part {STR_VAR_3}. Now, where were we...
Pause: Let's stop there. A story like this needs room to breathe.
Come back and I'll tell you what happened next.
Wait: You've heard everything I've got ready, {PLAYER}. The next episode needs another week of work.
Want to hear an old one again?
Done: Want to hear one of the old ones again?
ReplayEnd: Funny. Every time I tell it, I notice something new.
Bye: Then go make some history of your own. I'll be here.
CallBrendan: Do you ever listen to THE DEEP PAST? The history show, on the radio here in KANTO.
MAY and I had it on in PEWTER, and the host, DAN, said a trainer from JOHTO comes by the MUSEUM every week to hear his stories.
That's you, right? I knew it! Tell him to do one about HOENN's gyms next. Bye!

outro: That's every story I've got. For now.
History keeps happening, {PLAYER}. Mostly to people like you. I'll be here when there's more to tell.
